strengths: Rejects the all-konbini-are-24h stereotype with urban/rural and chain-level variation.
Labor shortage, franchise strain, and 2019 conflict prevent a “Japan loves convenience” myth.
Fact vs interpretation in the history section is exactly the editorial standard.
Closing treats late hours as a compromise, not a cultural performance.

issues.location: Train-shaped days — bathroom in one box
issues.problem: Customer toilets are not a standard konbini amenity. Treating them as part of the night-infrastructure package over-generalizes urban stores, especially small station boxes.
issues.suggestion: Do not list a bathroom as a given. Say restrooms exist at some locations and are not guaranteed.

issues.location: Night-store uses + 3 a.m. scenario — children’s/fever medicine
issues.problem: OTC medicine at konbini requires specific staffing and inventory. Presenting fever/children’s medicine as a typical 3 a.m. purchase overstates what the format does versus a drugstore.
issues.suggestion: Hedge or replace with drinks, cooling sheets, or “limited OTC at some stores.”

issues.location: Late Does Not Mean Every Store — 2024 noticeable minority
issues.problem: “Noticeable minority” across major chains sits next to Seven-Eleven’s ~6% figure and can sound like a larger national reversal than that chain’s number supports. Other chains have differed; the sentence blurs that.
issues.suggestion: Keep 7-Eleven’s 2026 figure hedged; make 2024 a qualitative “more stores allowed to close” rather than a cross-chain minority claim.
